Next door was an expensive [[eco hotel]] with solar panels and a garden on the roof. During the day, the girls lay on sunbeds at the [[beach club]] and bought cold lemonade at the [[beach bar]]. One afternoon they walked too far along the coast and saw a sign for a [[nudist]] beach, so they quickly turned around, giggling. Lisa's uncle was a member of the local [[yacht club]] and took them sailing on Thursday. That evening, the hotel next door held a [[pool party]], and the music was so loud they could hear it from their room. On their last night, they went to a [[beach party]] with a bonfire and danced until midnight. Anna promised herself she would come back next summer.

lessons.title: Shopping for a New Car
lessons.story: Anna's dad had been driving the same old [[hatchback]] for twelve years, and it was finally time for a new car. On Saturday, the whole family went to the [[auto show]] at the expo center to look at electric models. Dad read every [[crash test]] result before he would even sit in a car. Taras ignored the family cars and ran straight to the giant [[monster truck]] on display. Near the exit, members of a [[biker club]] in leather jackets were showing off their shiny old motorcycles. On the way home, a warning light came on, and the [[speedometer]] suddenly stopped working. Dad drove slowly to the nearest [[auto center]], where a mechanic fixed a loose wire in twenty minutes. While they waited, Taras watched an [[excavator]] digging across the road and said it was better than the whole show.

lessons.title: Mama's New Home Office
lessons.story: When Anna's mama started working remotely, she turned the spare bedroom into a [[home office]]. Her old [[laptop]] was too slow for video calls, so she bought a used [[desktop]] with a big screen. Taras helped her connect every [[cable]], although he mixed up two of them at first. She also ordered a small [[microphone]] because her colleagues said she sounded like she was underwater. The webcam had a digital [[zoom]], which Mama accidentally used in her first meeting, filling the screen with her nose. The internet kept dropping, so Dad called their [[provider]], who told him to move the [[router]] closer to her room. By Friday, the whole [[setup]] was working perfectly. Then the power went out, and Mama spent the afternoon working [[offline]] on documents she had saved earlier.

lessons.title: A Bad Day for Max's Laptop
lessons.story: On Monday morning, Max's [[task manager]] app reminded him that his essay was due at noon. Ten minutes later, his laptop froze in the middle of the last paragraph. It turned out to be a [[glitch]] caused by last night's [[update]] to his writing app. A [[reset]] of the app didn't help, but luckily he had made a [[backup]] on Sunday. Sofia, who studies IT, said the real problem was his old [[hardware]] and that he needed a memory [[upgrade]]. She also showed him a keyboard [[shortcut]] that saves the file whenever he presses it. Then the printer announced that it needed a new ink [[cartridge]]. So Max ran to the library and used the [[scanner]] to send his handwritten notes to the teacher. He handed in the essay five minutes before the deadline.

lessons.title: Grandpa Goes Online
lessons.story: Anna's grandpa wanted to find a recipe online, so she sat down to help him. He wasn't sure what a [[web browser]] was, so she explained that it is the program you use to open websites. When she opened her favorite [[browser]], a [[pop-up]] about cookies appeared, and Grandpa nearly closed the whole window. Next they checked his email, which was full of [[spam]] promising free money. Anna deleted it all and showed him how to type a web address, with a [[slash]] before the page name. They found a cooking [[wiki]] where thousands of people share family recipes. To save his favorite ones, Grandpa had to become a registered [[user]] and fill in his [[profile]]. He proudly chose a photo of his garden instead of his face. Then Anna used a [[template]] to make a neat recipe card for Grandma's birthday. She added a [[QR code]] to the back, and Grandma laughed when it opened Grandpa's new page.

lessons.title: Movie night at home
lessons.story: On Friday evening, Anna and Max couldn't agree on a [[genre]] for movie night. Max wanted [[sci-fi]], but Anna was in the mood for a light [[sitcom]]. In the end, they watched the [[trailer]] for a space adventure together. Then Taras found a [[preview]] online and got excited, because it was a [[remake]] of Dad's favorite old film. Just as the movie started, Max almost gave away a [[spoiler]] from a review he had read. Anna threw a pillow at him, and he promised to stay quiet. After that, the [[suspense]] kept everyone on the edge of their seats. When the credits rolled, Taras asked if they could download the [[soundtrack]]. Next Friday, Anna gets to choose the movie.

lessons.title: Life online
lessons.story: Last week, Anna's phone kept freezing, so she asked for help on a tech [[forum]]. At first, a [[troll]] replied with silly insults instead of advice. Anna ignored him, but the [[trolling]] continued under her post for hours. Finally, a [[moderator]] stepped in and deleted the rude comments. Then a user with thousands of [[followers|follower]] explained how to clear the phone's memory step by step. It worked, and Anna shared the tip with a [[hashtag]] so others could find it. Max sent her a [[meme]] about phones that never listen to their owners. Lisa replied with a dancing cat [[gif]], and Ira added a [[tag]] so the post would show up under "phone tips." Anna realized that a helpful online [[community]] is worth more than any app.

lessons.title: TV night at Grandma's
lessons.story: Every evening, Grandma and Grandpa argue about what to watch on TV. Grandpa never misses his favorite [[game show]], where people answer questions to win a car. Grandma prefers the [[talent show]], because she loves the young singers. Unfortunately, both programs are on during [[prime time]] on Tuesdays. Last Tuesday, Grandpa even skipped the cooking [[segment]] of the news just to keep the remote. Then Anna came over and explained how [[streaming]] works. She set up a [[streaming service]] on their TV so they could watch one program later. Now her grandparents have twice as much [[entertainment]] and no more arguments.

lessons.title: A gamer's evening
lessons.story: Max spends most Friday evenings [[gaming]] with his friends. Last Friday, he turned on his [[console]] and found that his [[controller]] wasn't working. Luckily, Sofia lent him hers, though she made him promise to be careful. They were playing a new [[RPG]], and its [[gameplay]] was surprisingly easy to learn. First, Max chose a knight as his [[avatar]] and joined his friends' [[squad]]. In the final battle, he pulled off a perfect [[combo]] and defeated the dragon. The screen showed that he had beaten his own [[high score]]. That night, Max told Sofia that he wants to become a [[game developer]] one day. Sofia laughed and said he should start by repairing his broken one first.

lessons.title: My first video blog
lessons.story: Anna decided to try [[blogging]] and make her first video about her hobbies. She talked about the [[anime]] she watches on weekends and the [[manga]] she reads before bed. Max lent her a small voice [[recorder]], because the sound on her phone was terrible. Editing was harder than she expected, and she spent an hour moving clips around the [[timeline]]. At the end, she asked viewers to check their sources and never to share [[fake news]]. The next day, her video had fifty views, and Taras proudly said that forty of them were his.

lessons.title: A night of celebrity life
lessons.story: Lisa won two tickets to a film premiere in Kyiv and invited Ira. There was so much [[hype]] around the event that the whole street was full of fans. The [[paparazzi]] were taking photos of everyone who walked down the red carpet. The girls weren't [[VIPs|VIP]], so they had to stand behind a fence. Still, when the lead actress came closer, Ira asked for her [[autograph]], and a huge [[bodyguard]] let her through. For a moment, Lisa could feel the [[glamour]] of [[showbiz]]. Later, a talent [[scout]] noticed Lisa's confident smile and gave her a business card. That evening, Lisa rewrote the [[bio]] on her profile: "Future actress."

lessons.title: Making an indie film
lessons.story: Sofia wants to be a [[filmmaker]], so this summer she made a short film with her friends. Max agreed to be the [[cameraman]], although he had never filmed anything before. They chose their grandparents' village as the [[setting]], because the old houses looked perfect for the story. Anna became the [[narrator]], and her calm voice tied all the scenes together. Sofia believes that good [[storytelling]] matters more than expensive equipment. For the music, she used songs by a local band that plays [[indie]]. Grandpa even found an old photo [[negative]] of the village from 1970 and printed it for the opening scene. In August, they showed the finished film at a [[drive-in]] outside the city. Everyone watched from their parents' cars and honked at the end instead of clapping.

lessons.title: A creepy fantasy film
lessons.story: On Halloween, Taras wanted to watch a fantasy movie with his big sister. Anna chose one with a brave [[hobbit]] and a wise [[elf]] who travel through a dark forest. Halfway through, a [[goblin]] stole their map, and Taras hid under a blanket. Then the heroes reached a castle where an old [[vampire]] lived, and the music became really [[creepy]]. Anna paused the movie when the castle's cook turned out to be a [[cannibal]], because she thought it was too scary. But Taras insisted he wasn't afraid and asked her to keep going. In the end, the little hero saved everyone, and Taras said he had been as brave as a [[superman]]. Still, he asked Anna to leave the hallway light on that night.

lessons.title: In the newsroom
lessons.story: Anna spent a week of work experience at a national [[broadcaster]] in Kyiv. On her first morning, the [[newsroom]] was louder than she had expected. Her job was to prepare a short news [[digest]] for the station's website. At lunch, a [[tabloid]] published a story about a [[scandal]] involving a famous football coach. Everyone wanted to report it, but the chief editor asked them to check the facts first. A [[correspondent]] in Lviv called and confirmed that the rumors were false. That evening, the editor wrote an [[editorial]] about why the [[mass media]] should not repeat gossip. Anna shared it on social [[media]], and Max replied, "Best first week ever!"

lessons.title: Learning to code
lessons.story: Max wanted to build a small [[bot]] that answers questions about his school timetable. His sister Sofia, a [[software engineer]], offered to help him on Saturday. First, she explained that every [[programmer]] makes mistakes, so he shouldn't panic. They wrote a simple [[algorithm]] that finds the next lesson for any day. Max tested it, but the [[output]] was always "Monday, 8:00." Sofia opened the [[log]] and found the problem: the program ignored the user's [[input]]. After fixing it, they designed a clean [[interface]] with two big buttons. Max even wrote a short [[manual]] so his classmates would know how to use it. By evening, his friends were sending it questions, and [[coding]] suddenly seemed much less scary.

lessons.title: Building a computer
lessons.story: Max decided to build his own computer instead of buying a new one. Anna's dad, who loves electronics, offered to help him choose each [[component]]. They spent an hour comparing prices for a [[processor]] and a graphics card. Dad explained that a modern [[chip]] contains billions of tiny switches. "Each [[transistor]] is smaller than a virus," he said. He also reminded Max that a single [[byte]] is made up of eight bits. The power supply was rated at 650 [[watts|watt]], which was enough for everything. When they finally turned it on, Max checked his [[ping]] and was delighted with the result. That night, he paid for cheap [[hosting]] and started planning a [[redesign]] of his old gaming blog.

lessons.title: A night of gaming
lessons.story: On Friday night, Lisa and Ira came to Anna's place for a gaming marathon. Ira had downloaded a [[mod]] that turned all the monsters into giant ducks. "[[LOL]], this is the best thing ever," Lisa wrote in the group chat. Around midnight, a strange message appeared, claiming that a [[hacker]] had taken over their account. Anna immediately texted Max's sister Sofia, who works in [[high-tech]]. Sofia replied that it was just a fake pop-up from a browser [[plug-in]]. She explained that real [[hacking]] rarely looks so dramatic. The girls deleted it and went back to their ducks. At three in the morning, the screen finally showed "[[game over]]," and everyone fell asleep on the sofa.

lessons.title: Computer problems
lessons.story: On Monday morning, Anna's laptop seemed to have a mind of its own. First, the [[touchpad]] stopped responding, and the [[cursor]] froze in the corner of the screen. She plugged in a mouse, but her [[login]] was rejected three times. Then she noticed that [[caps lock]] was on, so every password she typed was wrong. Once she got in, a single [[misclick]] almost deleted her history essay. She pressed [[print screen]] to save the error message and sent it to Max. He told her to run the [[antivirus]] and do a full [[restart]]. It worked, and even her [[screensaver]] with the family dog came back. Later, she discovered that the [[spam filter]] had hidden Max's long email full of tips.

lessons.title: Shopping online
lessons.story: Anna's mama had a birthday coming up, so Anna decided to shop online. After an hour of [[scrolling]], she found a lovely scarf already saved on her [[wishlist]]. The store was new, and Lisa had sent her an [[invite code]] for a discount. However, the discount didn't appear when she tried to pay. Anna clicked the [[live chat]] button, but only a [[chatbot]] answered, with useless replies. Finally, a real assistant explained that she had forgotten to tick a [[checkbox]] under the code. With one [[swipe]], she confirmed the payment on her phone. Two days later, mama opened the parcel and loved the scarf.

lessons.title: Playing video games
lessons.story: Taras got a [[gamepad]] for his birthday, and Max promised to teach him a flying game. The [[joystick]] felt strange at first, and Taras kept crashing his plane into mountains. His first attempt was an [[epic fail]], but he refused to give up. Max showed him a popular [[streamer]] who explains the game clearly. During her [[livestream]], she shared a [[cheat code]] for extra fuel, but Max said real pilots don't cheat. After two hours of practice, Taras managed to [[level up]] three times. Then they tried [[multiplayer]] together against kids from all over the world. By the end of the evening, Taras's name appeared on the weekly [[leaderboard]], and he proudly sent a photo of it to grandma.

lessons.title: Life on social media
lessons.story: Last week, Ira posted a video of her dog stealing a sandwich from the table. By the next morning, it had become an [[internet meme]] that everyone at school was sharing. Anna's [[repost]] alone got hundreds of likes, and the original collected thousands of [[retweets|retweet]]. Then someone shared an old clip of Ira singing with a silly [[photo filter]] on her face. Ira laughed and admitted it was pure [[cringe]]. Soon, however, a [[bot account]] and a few classmates began posting nasty comments under every post she made. Anna knew this was [[cyberbullying]], so she reported the comments and told their teacher. When the class chat filled up with jokes about it, Max politely asked everyone to move the [[off-topic]] to another group. Meanwhile, Ira's dad found good advice on an [[internet forum]], and by Friday the comments had stopped.

lessons.title: My Brother Wants Fame
lessons.story: At breakfast, Taras announced that he was going to become a famous [[youtuber]]. Last month he had wanted to be a [[tiktoker]], but now he said short dances were not his style. He borrowed Anna's old phone and filmed his first [[vlog]] about his school day. Max, who follows a [[vlogger]] from Lviv, gave him some tips about light and sound. Then Taras decided that a [[prank video]] would get more views, so he hid a plastic spider in Dad's shoe. Dad screamed, laughed, and called him the biggest [[prankster]] in the family. In the end, the video got only twelve views, mostly from the grandparents. Still, Taras was happy, and he celebrated by downloading a new [[sticker pack]] with dancing spiders.

lessons.title: Interviewing a Blogger
lessons.story: For a school assignment, Anna and Lisa had to interview someone who works online. Lisa wrote to a [[food blogger]] who reviews cafés in Kyiv, but she never answered. Anna tried a [[fashion blogger]], a [[travel blogger]], and even a [[beauty blogger]] with a huge audience, but they were all too busy. Then Ira mentioned that her cousin is a [[video blogger]] who films short documentaries about small towns. He also calls himself a [[lifestyle blogger]] because he talks about cooking, books, and slow mornings. "I'm not really an [[influencer]]," he told them on a video call. "I just share things I find interesting." The girls turned the interview into a [[blogpost]] for the school website. A week later, Ira's cousin shared a link to it on his [[travel blog]], and their teacher was very impressed.

lessons.title: Grandpa's Old Music Collection
lessons.story: While cleaning the attic, Anna found a box of Grandpa's old music. Every [[compact disc]] was still in its original case, and some even had price labels on them. There was also an [[audio disc]] from a language course that Grandma had used in the nineties. Anna's favorite album had a [[bonus track]] that she had never heard online. Her laptop had no disc drive, so Max brought an external one and opened a free [[media player]]. When the music started, Grandpa said it sounded better than on his old [[audio player]]. Max copied everything onto a drive with one [[terabyte]] of space, which was far more than they needed. Grandpa laughed and said his first computer had only a few hundred [[kilobytes|kilobyte]] of memory. Finally, Anna saved a [[preset]] with extra bass for Grandpa's favorite songs, and he listened to them all evening.

lessons.title: Mom's First Office Day
lessons.story: On Monday, Anna's mom started a new job at an insurance company. At the entrance, a security guard gave her a [[badge]] with her photo on it. She had worried about the [[dress code]], but most people were wearing jeans and simple sweaters. The [[office manager]], a cheerful woman named Olena, showed her the kitchen and the [[meeting room]]. Next, someone from [[HR]] asked her to sign a few forms about her salary and vacation days. Her [[supervisor]] gave her a [[checklist]] for her first week and a thick folder with every company [[guideline]]. Mom was going to work in the [[back office]], handling documents rather than talking to customers. By lunchtime, a colleague had already told her she was a real [[ace]] with spreadsheets. That evening, she told the family that her first day had gone much better than she had expected.

lessons.title: Sofia's First Big Client
lessons.story: Last year, Max's sister Sofia left her job in the public [[sector]] to try [[freelance]] design. Being a [[freelancer]] was scary at first, because work did not come every month. Last week, though, she finally got a big [[project]] from a chain of bakeries. Before she started, the [[client]] sent her a [[contract]] to read and sign. They agreed to have a [[one-on-one]] call every Friday to discuss her progress. After the first call, the manager sent her some honest [[feedback]] about the colors in her logo. Sofia made the changes and even offered [[one-to-one]] training for their staff on the new design. The bakery loved the idea, and the extra money gave her confidence a real [[boost]].

lessons.title: Ira at the Call Center
lessons.story: Ira got a summer job at a [[call center]] that answers questions for a phone [[service center]]. On her first shift, she worked as an [[operator]], helping customers with broken screens and lost chargers. In the morning, her computer froze, so she called the system [[administrator]]. He was busy, so another [[admin]] came over and restarted everything. He explained that a [[script]] ran every night to back up the customer records, and it had crashed. During lunch, her manager said that patience was the most important [[soft skill]] in this job. She also offered Ira some free [[coaching]] on how to calm down angry callers. In the afternoon, Ira faced a [[dilemma]]: an old man needed help, but her shift was ending. She stayed ten extra minutes, and he thanked her warmly. Just as she hung up, Anna texted that she was waiting outside with ice cream, which was perfect [[timing]].

lessons.title: A Busy Office Week
lessons.story: Anna's dad works on the fifth floor of a large [[business center]] near the river. This week, his [[project manager]] announced that the company was moving to a smaller office. Everyone had to clear their desks, and the old [[shredder]] worked nonstop from morning till evening. On Wednesday, a [[consultant]] arrived to help them organize the move. She had worked in [[consulting]] for twenty years and seemed to have a solution for every problem. On Thursday, she ran a short [[seminar]] about working in shared spaces. At the end, she handed out a colorful [[booklet]] with tips on keeping desks tidy. Dad brought it home, and Mom joked that he should read it twice.

lessons.title: Our New Startup
lessons.story: Max and Anna decided to launch a small [[startup]] that delivers homemade snacks to students. Max called himself the [[founder]], but Anna reminded him that the idea was hers. They spent a weekend writing a [[business plan]] at Grandma's kitchen table. Their [[business model]] was simple: students would pay a small monthly fee for weekly deliveries. The only problem was that they had almost no [[capital]], just their savings from summer jobs. Then Grandma offered to bake the cookies herself and become their [[business partner]]. After the first month, they made a tiny [[profit]] of about fifty dollars. Grandma said it was a [[win-win]] deal: they got great cookies, and she got two helpers in her garden.

lessons.title: The marketing team
lessons.story: Anna started a summer internship with the [[marketing]] team at a small juice company. On Monday, the [[product manager]] explained that they were launching a new mango drink. Anna's first job was to help write a [[press release]] for local news websites. Max, who works part-time as a concert [[promoter]], gave her some tips on getting people's attention. The team also planned a weekend [[promotion]]: buy one bottle and get the second one free. Anna designed a colorful [[flyer]] that students could hand out near the university. Meanwhile, the [[email marketing]] campaign reached thousands of customers at once. On Friday, Anna saw the mango drink on a huge [[billboard]] by the highway and sent a proud photo to her mama.

lessons.title: Import and export
lessons.story: Anna's dad works for a small company that sells Ukrainian honey abroad. Honey has become an important [[export]] for their region in the last few years. Last month, a large [[cargo]] of honey jars left Odesa by ship. A [[distributor]] in Poland agreed to deliver the jars to stores across the country. One big [[retailer]] even wanted to sell the honey on its website. At dinner, Taras asked why oil is sold by the [[barrel]] but honey isn't. Dad laughed and explained that oil [[trading]] works very differently from selling food. He also mentioned that the company's new delivery truck was an [[import]] from Germany. He had found it at an [[auction]] for half the usual price. Grandpa said the whole family should be proud, and Taras immediately asked for a free jar.

lessons.title: A record year
lessons.story: It was a record year for Lisa's family, and everyone wanted to celebrate. Her mom worked as the [[art director]] on a small Ukrainian comedy film. Surprisingly, the movie did really well at the [[box office]] all summer. Her dad, an [[economist]], wrote a simple book about saving money for teenagers. To his surprise, it became a [[bestseller]] in just three months. In the fall, he was invited to talk about it at a big book [[expo]] in Lviv. Even Lisa had good news: she remembered fifty digits of [[pi]] and won the school math contest. At the party, Anna joked that the family would soon need a bigger shelf for all their prizes.

lessons.title: Banking online
lessons.story: Anna's grandpa used to go to the bank every week to pay his bills. This year, Anna decided to teach him how to use [[online banking]] on his phone. Grandma had already tried [[internet banking]] on her laptop, but she found the website confusing. Anna showed them that their card even gave them [[cashback]] on groceries. Grandpa still had questions, so they called his [[account manager]] at the bank. She was very patient, even though she usually works with [[business clients|business client]] like shops and cafes. By the end of the week, Grandpa had paid all his bills alone. He even made his first [[preorder]]: a new fishing book that comes out in May. Now he calls Anna after every payment to tell her how easy it was.

lessons.title: A new office job
lessons.story: Max's sister Sofia had wanted to work in the [[IT sector]] for a long time. In March, she went to a job fair at the [[expo center]] and talked to a dozen companies. She had prepared for it by watching a free [[webinar]] about job interviews. One small company liked her [[résumé]], especially the mobile game she had built as a [[side project]]. During the interview, the manager said the team never worked late on weekends, which Sofia saw as a real [[green flag]]. On her first day, she got a laptop, a quiet [[workspace]] near the window, and a bright yellow [[stapler]]. The old [[copier]] broke twice before lunch, but her new colleagues just laughed about it. On Friday, the whole office went bowling for [[team building]], and Sofia won the first game.

lessons.title: Planning an offline event
lessons.story: Ira's online book club decided to hold its first [[offline event]] in a cafe in Kyiv. Ira's cousin, who works as a [[copywriter]], offered to help with the invitation. She said that good [[copywriting]] is about short, warm sentences, not fancy words. Lisa, the club's unofficial [[content manager]], planned social media posts for every day that week. Anna's mama knew a [[brand manager]] at a local bakery, and he agreed to bring free cookies. In return, the bakery wanted a little [[publicity]]. So the club hung a large [[banner]] with the bakery's logo above the cafe door. Then a [[PR specialist]] from a publishing house heard about the event and offered to send a young author. Her boss, the [[PR manager]], said it was cheaper than an ad and great for [[PR]]. On Saturday, sixty people came, and the cookies were gone within an hour.

lessons.title: On the stock market
lessons.story: Max's economics teacher started a stock market game for the class. Max decided to be a careful [[investor]] and bought shares in three companies. Ira acted as a [[trader]], buying and selling almost every hour. Lisa played the class [[broker]], so everyone had to send their orders through her. Every morning, they checked how the main stock market [[index]] had changed overnight. In one lesson, the teacher explained how a budget [[deficit]] grows when a country spends more than it earns. Some countries, she added, owe more than a [[trillion]] dollars. On Thursday, Ira put all her money into [[bitcoin]], and its price fell sharply that afternoon. She called it a total [[collapse]], although she had only lost imaginary money. On Friday, the teacher did a quick [[audit]] of everyone's accounts and announced that slow, careful Max had won.

lessons.title: A millionaire's banquet
lessons.story: Last summer, Anna worked as a waitress at a fancy hotel in Kyiv. One evening, the hotel hosted a [[banquet]] for a local [[millionaire]] who was celebrating his sixtieth birthday. He arrived with a security [[escort]], which made the whole staff nervous. Anna stood at the door and offered every guest a [[welcome drink]]: fresh juice or [[prosecco]]. Later, she carried silver plates of black [[caviar]] around the room. The manager reminded her that every guest was a [[VIP client]], so she had to smile all night. At midnight, the guests moved to the [[lounge bar]], and Anna could finally sit down. The next morning, she found a thank-you note and a big tip from the birthday man himself.

lessons.title: A day at the office
lessons.story: Anna has a summer internship at a small company in Kyiv. On Monday morning, the printer ran out of [[toner]] just before an important meeting. Then everyone heard that the [[big boss]] was visiting the office that afternoon. Anna was trying to finish a presentation, answer emails and order lunch at the same time, but [[multitasking]] only made her slower. Max, who works there as an [[IT specialist]], fixed the printer in five minutes. Meanwhile, the [[web designer]] was redrawing the new homepage, and the [[web developer]] was building it with a simple [[drag-and-drop]] editor. The [[webmaster]] noticed that half of the text on the site was [[copy-paste]] from an old brochure, so Anna rewrote it quickly. At the meeting, the boss spoke for an hour about budgets, targets and other [[blah-blah]]. But at the end, she praised the team's new website, and Anna smiled all the way home.

lessons.title: Working in media
lessons.story: Max's sister Sofia works at a small agency that creates [[media content]] for local businesses. This month she is leading a [[media project]] about young people in Kyiv. The client wanted more [[video content]], so the team planned a [[photoshoot]] and a series of short films. A [[photojournalist]] friend agreed to take pictures by the river and on the busy streets. For the website, Sofia recorded a [[video interview]] with Anna about student life. She also wanted to try [[podcasting]], so she turned their chat into the first episode of a podcast. Because some guests lived in other cities, the panel discussion was held in an [[online format]]. Before anything went public, a [[media expert]] did a careful [[fact-check]] of every number. She found one mistake, and Sofia fixed it just in time. When the project launched on Friday, the client called to say it was their best campaign yet.

lessons.title: Friday night at the pub
lessons.story: On Friday, Anna's dad took the family to a cozy pub near their house to celebrate his birthday. They arrived during [[happy hour]], so the place was busy and loud. Dad ordered a pint of local [[ale]], and his old friend chose a cold [[lager]]. Anna and Taras had warm apple [[cider]], which tasted like autumn. In the back room, Taras tried [[darts]] for the first time and hit the board only once. Grandpa, meanwhile, beat everyone at [[snooker]] and looked very proud of himself. Anna loved the [[vibe]]: old photos on the walls, quiet music and lots of laughter. Then Mama brought out a birthday cake she had secretly made that morning. She had whipped the cream with her new electric [[mixer]] and added a little coffee [[liqueur]] to it. Dad said it was the best part of the evening.

lessons.title: At the hotel bar
lessons.story: For their fiftieth anniversary, Anna's grandparents invited the whole family to a hotel in Lviv. In the evening, everyone met at the hotel bar, where a friendly [[bartender]] was polishing glasses. Grandpa, as always, asked for a small [[cognac]], and Grandma chose a classic [[martini]] with an olive. Dad couldn't choose between [[whiskey]] and [[bourbon]], so the bartender patiently explained the difference. Mama ordered a [[margarita]], while her cousin had a [[gin]] with lime. A man at the next table asked for [[tequila]], but the bar had just run out. Anna, who doesn't drink alcohol, asked for a [[tonic]] with lemon and ice. Then the bartender made Taras a special alcohol-free [[cocktail]] with mint and berries and called it "The Lviv Sunset." Taras was delighted, and Grandpa raised his glass to fifty wonderful years.

lessons.title: A costume party
lessons.story: Lisa got an [[invite]] to Ira's costume party and immediately texted Anna. The party was in a big old house, and Ira's aunt, a professional event [[coordinator]], had organized everything. Anna came as a [[pirate]], with a paper hat and a fake parrot on her shoulder. Max arrived as a [[zombie]], and his makeup was so realistic that Lisa screamed when she saw him. Ira's cousin from Scotland wore a real [[kilt]], which everyone thought was a costume. The [[catering]] was excellent: tiny pizzas, fresh fruit and a chocolate fountain. In the garden, there was even a small [[carousel]] for the younger kids. Later, everyone sang [[karaoke]], and Max's zombie version of a love song won first prize. At midnight, Ira threw [[confetti]] over the dance floor. Three days later, Anna was still finding [[glitter]] from Lisa's costume in her hair.

lessons.title: The town festival
lessons.story: Every summer, the small town where Anna's grandparents live holds a music [[fest]] by the river. This year it began with a colorful [[carnival]], with dancers and giant puppets parading down the main street. Later, a group of Mexican students turned the town square into a real [[fiesta]], with bright flags and loud trumpets. Taras was hungry all day, so the family kept going back to the [[snack bar]] for corn and hot dogs. In the evening, Anna and Max watched a [[stand-up]] show by a young local comedian, and Grandpa laughed louder than anyone. At the end, the organizers held a [[giveaway]], and Taras won a bicycle with his lucky ticket. He rode it home proudly, ringing the bell all the way.

lessons.title: Our band's first gig
lessons.story: Max and his friends have a small rock band, and last Saturday they played their first gig. Lisa is the band's [[vocalist]], and Max plays guitar and is the main [[songwriter]]. When the local club posted the [[lineup]] for the night, they were amazed to see their name right before a well-known group. Ira jokingly called herself their [[tour manager]], although the "tour" was just one bus ride across Kyiv. To everyone's surprise, the show was [[sold out]] by Friday. Backstage, Max was so nervous that he forgot the [[intro]] to their first song during the sound check. Then the [[MC]] announced their name, and the crowd started clapping. Somehow Max's fingers found the right notes, and Lisa's voice filled the room. It wasn't a perfect [[live show]], but nobody cared, and Anna cheered the loudest.

lessons.title: In the record shop
lessons.story: On Saturday, Anna went with her dad to a small record shop in the center of Kyiv. Dad went straight to the [[funk]] section and started telling her about the music of his youth. Anna found an old [[blues]] album and decided to buy it for Grandpa. The owner, a cheerful man with a gray beard, said this album was recorded in [[stereo]] and sounded much better on [[vinyl]] than online. He also mentioned that a local band was celebrating the [[release]] of their first album in the shop that evening. Anna and Dad stayed for the concert and bought some [[merch]], a T-shirt with the band's logo. On Sunday, Grandpa played the record three times and danced with Grandma in the kitchen.

lessons.title: The dance competition
lessons.story: Anna and Max entered a dance competition at the youth center in Kyiv. They had practiced their [[salsa]] for weeks, but on the day, Max was so nervous that his hands were shaking. The first couple performed a dramatic [[tango]], and the crowd went wild. Next came a lively [[samba]] by two girls in bright costumes with feathers. Before Anna and Max's turn, Lisa sang a [[duet]] with her cousin, and Ira played a short violin [[solo]]. Then a jazz [[trio]] from the music school played while the judges took notes. When the music finally started, Anna and Max forgot their fears and danced better than ever. They didn't win first place, but the judges called them "the happiest [[duo]] of the night."

lessons.title: The school concert
lessons.story: Taras's school was preparing for its spring concert, and the music room was full of noise. One boy was practicing the [[banjo]], while two girls tried to play the [[trombone]] without laughing. Taras had chosen the [[ukulele]] because it was small and easy to carry. His classmate Dan, on the other hand, could barely lift his huge [[tuba]]. At the final rehearsal, the teacher asked Max, who was helping out, to play [[bass]] for the band. Halfway through the first song, one of Taras's strings broke with a loud noise. Everyone froze, and Taras turned bright red. "Well, that was a total [[fail]]," he joked, and the whole room burst out laughing. Max lent him a spare string, and on the night of the concert, everything went perfectly.

lessons.title: A night at the ballet
lessons.story: For Grandma's birthday, the family bought tickets to the [[ballet]] at the opera house in Kyiv. Anna had wanted to see a [[musical]] instead, but Grandma had dreamed about this evening for months. Before the show, a well-known [[tenor]] sang two short songs, and Grandpa whispered that his voice gave him goosebumps. Then the [[maestro]] raised his hand, and the orchestra began to play. The lead [[ballerina]] seemed to float across the stage like a feather. During the break, Anna read in the program that the theater's [[repertoire]] included over thirty performances this season. She also noticed that a famous piano [[sonata]] would be performed there next week. At home, Grandma was so moved that she wrote a [[sonnet]] about the evening and read it aloud at dinner. Even Anna had to admit that it was a perfect night.

lessons.title: At the art exhibition
lessons.story: On Saturday, Anna and Sofia went to an art exhibition in a glass [[pavilion]] in the city park. Outside, a young artist was finishing a giant [[mural]] of sunflowers on a wall. Inside, a [[sculptor]] was showing small figures made from old bicycle parts. Sofia's favorite room was full of drawings by an [[illustrator]] who works on children's books. Anna loved a corner with [[retro]] posters that looked like they came straight from the seventies. While they were looking at them, a serious man with a notebook stopped next to them. He turned out to be an [[art critic]] writing a review for a local magazine. He asked the girls which piece they liked best, and Sofia pointed to a drawing of a sleepy cat. A week later, Anna found the review online, and it quoted "a young visitor" who loved the cat.

lessons.title: Beats at the club
lessons.story: For Lisa's eighteenth birthday, the friends went to a small club near the river. The DJ started the night with a smooth [[mix]] of old soul and [[R&B]] hits. Later, the music changed to relaxed [[reggae]], and Ira tried to teach Max how to move to the beat. Around midnight, the lights turned blue and loud [[techno]] filled the room. Then the DJ surprised everyone with a [[remix]] of Lisa's favorite song from her childhood. Max, who never dances, jumped onto the small stage and performed a funny [[freestyle]] rap about Lisa. Everyone cheered, and Lisa laughed so hard that she nearly cried. It was, she said, the best birthday she had ever had.

lessons.title: The punk years
lessons.story: While cleaning the attic, Anna found a box of old photos and cassette tapes. "That's me at sixteen," laughed her dad, pointing to a boy with spiky green hair. Back then, he listened to nothing but [[punk]] and dreamed of becoming a famous [[rocker]]. He even started a [[punk rock]] band with two friends from his street. Mama, on the other hand, used to be a [[goth]] who wore only black clothes and dark lipstick. Then Grandma showed them a photo of herself as a young [[hippie]] with flowers in her hair. Taras couldn't stop laughing, especially when he heard that Grandpa had loved [[heavy metal]]. That evening, the whole family played the old tapes and danced around the living room.

lessons.title: Casino night at home
lessons.story: For Sofia's birthday, Max turned their living room into a pretend [[casino]] for one night. Nobody used real money, because Max believed that [[gambling]] was a terrible way to lose your savings. Instead, every guest got a bag of chocolate coins at the door. Lisa and Ira sat down at the card table and tried to learn [[poker]] from Max's dad. Anna preferred [[blackjack]] because the rules were easier to understand. In one game, the [[joker]] could replace any card, and Taras kept forgetting what that meant. In the corner, an old [[pinball]] machine that Dad had repaired was beeping and flashing all evening. At the end of the night, Sofia hit the [[jackpot]] and won the biggest box of chocolates.

lessons.title: A weekend of shows
lessons.story: Anna wanted to give her little brother Taras the best weekend of his school break. On Friday evening, they watched an amazing [[light show]] on the old buildings by the river. On Saturday morning, they joined the crowds at a colorful [[parade]] through the city center. In the afternoon, they went to an [[ice show]], where skaters dressed as cartoon characters spun across the rink. Afterwards, they warmed up with hot chocolate at a cozy [[art cafe]] full of paintings and old lamps. The cafe also sold [[handmade]] gifts, and Taras bought a tiny painted [[matryoshka]] for Grandma. At the next table, a woman was teaching kids to fold paper cranes, and Taras spent an hour learning [[origami]]. On Sunday night, the weekend ended with a [[fire show]] on the beach, and Taras said it was the best weekend ever.

lessons.title: A school photo project
lessons.story: Anna's [[photo club]] gave everyone the same task: a [[photo project]] about their own neighborhood. Since Taras switched to [[homeschooling]] this year, Mama let him help and called it his [[art project]] for the month. Max brought his [[drone]] to shoot the park from above. The views looked amazing, but when Anna zoomed in too far, she could see every single [[pixel]]. Her close-up of Grandpa was completely out of [[focus]], so she had to take it again. In the end, the club chose her second try, a warm [[photo portrait]] of Grandpa feeding pigeons, as the best picture of the month. Taras proudly told everyone that he had held the bread.

lessons.title: At the art museum
lessons.story: On a rainy Saturday, Anna took her grandparents to the city art museum. Grandma went straight to the hall of French [[impressionism]], where soft light seemed to dance on every canvas. She explained that each [[impressionist]] tried to catch a single moment of light outdoors. Grandpa was confused by [[cubism]]. "Why does this woman have three eyes?" he whispered. In the next room, giant soup cans and comic book faces introduced them to [[pop art]]. The last hall surprised everyone with photos of [[street art]] from Kyiv's walls. Next to them, a big screen showed [[pixel art]] by young game designers. Grandpa admitted that the little square characters were his favorite part of the day.

lessons.title: Grandma writes a book
lessons.story: Grandma has always wanted to write a book, and this year she finally started. It is [[nonfiction]]: true stories from her village, mixed with the [[folklore]] her own grandmother used to tell. Anna helped her type the chapters, and Max's sister Sofia, a young [[essayist]] for a student magazine, read the first draft. Sofia was honest and said the opening chapter needed a complete [[rewrite]]. Grandma grumbled, but she spent a whole week on it. To relax, she wrote a short [[haiku]] about the cherry tree outside her window and put it at the start of the book. Last month, a small local [[publisher]] agreed to print it. "It won't join the great [[canon]] of literature," Grandma laughed, "but my great-grandchildren will read it."

lessons.title: Taras's birthday party
lessons.story: When Taras turned five, the family argued for weeks about his party. Dad suggested [[laser tag]], until Mama reminded him that the guests were preschoolers. A day at the [[aquapark]] seemed too cold for November, and [[minigolf]] would bore the little ones. In the end, they booked the party room at the [[bowling club]] near their home, with light balls and bumpers for small kids. The real star was a hired [[acrobat]] who flipped across the room and spun a [[hula hoop]] on each arm. Dressed as a cowboy, she caught a toy horse with a [[lasso]], and the kids screamed with joy. Taras got a glowing [[yo-yo]] from Anna and a fidget [[spinner]] from Max. But when Grandpa rolled in a shiny red [[tricycle]], Taras forgot everything else and rode it around until the party ended.

lessons.title: Game night with Grandpa
lessons.story: Every Friday, Anna visits her grandparents for game night. Grandpa starts the evening with a [[sudoku]] from the newspaper, which he usually finishes in ten minutes. Then he brings out the old wooden [[backgammon]] board he has had since he was a student. Anna rolled double sixes again and again, but Grandpa kept a perfect [[poker face]], so she never knew if he was worried. Grandma said that luck like that is exactly how people lose all their money at an [[online casino]]: they think it will never end. Sure enough, Anna's luck ran out, and Grandpa won the last game. She just shrugged and said, "Oh well, [[c'est la vie]]." They agreed to split the dishes [[fifty-fifty]] and to play [[croquet]] in the garden as soon as spring came.

lessons.title: A night out in clubs
lessons.story: To celebrate the end of their exams, Anna, Max, Lisa, and Ira planned a night out, and each of them chose one place. Ira took them first to a cozy [[jazz club]], where an old trio played quietly by candlelight. Max then dragged everyone to a loud [[rock club]] with sticky floors and a crowd in black T-shirts. Lisa preferred the [[disco club]] next door, where the [[deejay]] played only hits from the seventies. Anna had tickets for a [[techno concert]] in an old factory, but they arrived too late. The main [[techno DJ]] had already finished his two-hour [[DJ set]], and the staff were packing up. On the way back, they passed a dark [[techno club]] with a long line outside, but nobody had the energy to wait. They ended the night at a tiny [[karaoke club]], where Max sang so badly that everyone laughed until two in the morning.

lessons.title: Max's band needs help
lessons.story: Max and three friends have a [[cover band]] that plays old hits at school parties. In September their [[bassist]] moved to Lviv, so they urgently needed someone new. Anna's dad, who once played in a student [[jazz band]], offered to help with rehearsals. He also brought Sofia, a talented [[saxophonist]] from her music school, and suddenly they sounded almost like a [[big band]] from an old movie. Finding a new [[bass guitarist]] was harder, because the only boy who came wanted to play songs by his favorite [[boy band]]. Dad made them practice every song with a [[metronome]], since the drummer kept speeding up. At the winter concert, Lisa sang one song alone, and the crowd cheered so loudly that she joked about becoming a [[solo artist]]. Max just smiled, because he had learned the bass lines himself.

lessons.title: Music on a road trip
lessons.story: On the long drive to the grandparents' village, the family could not agree on music. Taras wanted [[K-pop]], because he had learned a whole dance from one video. Anna put on her favorite [[indie rock]] playlist, but Mama said it was too sad for a sunny day. Mama chose cheerful [[pop rock]] from the nineties, and Dad switched to old [[rhythm and blues]] as soon as she fell asleep. When Anna teased him, Dad confessed that he had been an [[emo]] at fifteen, with black nail polish and long bangs. Then Anna played a [[dubstep]] track from Max, which made the car shake and woke Mama up at once. Taras announced that he would be a famous [[hip-hop artist]] one day, not some sweet [[pop idol]]. Finally, they all agreed on an old [[rock opera]] that lasted almost as long as the trip. By the time they arrived, everyone was singing the final song together.

lessons.title: The Street Dance Battle
lessons.story: On Saturday, Max took Anna to a [[street dance]] event in a park in Kyiv. Someone had placed a huge [[boombox]] in the middle of the square, and the music was loud enough to shake the trees. First came a [[rap battle]], where two guys traded clever lines about cold coffee and late buses. Then a girl started a [[beatbox]] rhythm with nothing but her mouth and a microphone. Max's sister Sofia was already warming up for the [[dance battle]], since she had been practicing [[breakdance]] for months. Her opponent was a confident [[break dancer]] who spun on one hand and made the crowd scream. Sofia answered with a surprising mix of moves: a bit of [[flamenco]] footwork, a silly [[cha-cha-cha]] step, and a perfect freeze at the end. When someone in the crowd shouted for [[twerking]], she just laughed and kept to her own style. The judges couldn't decide, so they declared a tie, and the two dancers shook hands. On the way home, Anna admitted that she wanted to take lessons too.

lessons.title: Festival Weekend
lessons.story: Anna's grandparents live in a small town in the mountains, and this weekend the town was hosting its first [[jazz fest]]. On Friday, Grandpa tried to listen to the festival news, but the [[radio signal]] kept fading in and out. Finally, he caught a [[radio interview]] with the organizer, who promised a [[laser show]] over the lake on Saturday. Grandma, however, was more interested in her favorite [[radio drama]], which she never misses. Anna and Max, who had come to visit, decided to go to the [[night show]] by the water. The lights were amazing, and a crew from a [[travel show]] was filming the whole thing for TV. After that, the friends stayed for the [[late show]], a comedy set by local musicians. It felt like a live [[sketch show]], with jokes about rain, grandmas, and lost tickets. When they got home, Grandma was still awake, and she wanted to hear every detail.

lessons.title: A New Film
lessons.story: Lisa has been obsessed with a fantasy book series ever since Ira told her it was a [[must-read]]. The original copies sold out years ago, but last month a [[reprint]] finally appeared in the bookstore near her school. Now the studio has released a [[teaser]] for the film version, and the whole [[fandom]] is going crazy online. Lisa even writes [[fan fiction]] about the minor characters, and hundreds of people read it every week. On opening night, she and Ira went to the [[multiplex]] in a homemade [[cosplay]] of the two heroines. A woman in the lobby joked that Lisa walked like a [[top model]] in her long silver cloak. The movie was better than they expected, and the [[plot twist]] in the last ten minutes left the audience silent. Ira's dad filmed them in their costumes outside, so now they have a funny [[home video]] of the evening. Lisa says she will watch it again when the sequel comes out.

lessons.title: Learning a Language
lessons.story: At the start of the semester, Anna's English teacher handed out the [[syllabus]] and announced a project on everyday language. Anna chose to compare the way her grandparents talk with the way her friends text. Her grandparents speak a village [[dialect]], while Max and Lisa use so much online [[slang]] that Mama rarely understands them. Anna watched a video [[tutorial]] on how to record interviews and started asking questions. She found that some words have no exact English [[equivalent]], so she had to explain them with examples. In other cases, a simple [[synonym]] worked, but it often missed a small [[nuance]] of feeling. Her teacher also lent her an old [[paperback]] about word history, which showed how many English words come from [[Latin]]. The hardest part was the presentation, because it started with five minutes of [[small talk]] with a visiting teacher from Canada. Anna was nervous, but she made the guest laugh with a joke about her grandfather's favorite word. In the end, she got the highest grade in the class.

lessons.title: Help with Math
lessons.story: Taras had a geometry test on Monday, so Anna offered to help him on Sunday afternoon. He said he preferred [[algebra]], because numbers seemed easier than shapes. Anna started with a glass of water and dropped an ice [[cube]] into it to explain volume. Then she showed him a can of beans and asked him to measure the [[cylinder]] with a ruler. "Its [[radius]] is four centimeters and three [[millimeters|millimeter]]," Taras said proudly. Next, she asked him to draw an [[oval]] and a [[spiral]] without looking at the paper, which made them both laugh. Mama brought his cold medicine and reminded him that one tablet of 200 [[milligrams|milligram]] was enough. Before bed, he took an online quiz that claimed to measure his [[IQ]], and he announced that he was a genius. The next day, he got a B plus, which he called proof of his genius.

lessons.title: University Life
lessons.story: Anna is in her first year at university in Kyiv, and her history course is mostly online. Every week she logs in to the student [[portal]] to download the next [[module]] and check her grades. This month's topic was how the city changed at the turn of the [[millennium]]. To find old photos, Anna and Max visited the city [[archive]], where a friendly librarian brought out boxes of maps and an old [[atlas]]. The librarian, a quiet [[intellectual]] with thick glasses, seemed to know every street from memory. Meanwhile, Max was proud of his ninety-day [[streak]] in a language app, which he checked even in the reading room. Anna's project was chosen for the university exhibition, which carries some [[prestige]] in her department. At the end of the semester, she received a [[certificate]] with her name in gold letters. She gave a copy to the librarian to say thank you.

lessons.title: Trouble at School
lessons.story: Last month, a new boy joined Taras's class after moving back from Canada. At first, the language [[barrier]] made it hard for him to answer questions quickly. He loved computers and robots, so some classmates started calling him a [[geek]] as if it were an insult. One day, a few boys played a [[prank]] on him by hiding his backpack during the break. That evening, someone posted a photo of him online with the word "[[loser]]" on it, and Taras knew this was [[bullying]], not a joke. He showed the post to their teacher, who said that every online [[hater]] counts on other people staying silent. The next day in biology, she was explaining how a [[nerve]] sends signals to the brain, and she asked the new boy to help with the model. Then she talked to the class about how a [[stereotype]] can hide who someone really is. She said courage was the [[attribute]] she admired most, and she thanked Taras in front of everyone. By Friday, the new boy had joined the school robotics club, and Taras had joined it too.

lessons.title: Homework for every subject
lessons.story: On Sunday, Taras asks Anna to help with his homework, which seems to cover every subject. First, he has to draw a [[pentagon]] and count the lines that connect its corners. Anna shows him how to draw a [[diagonal]] from one corner to another. Next comes English: he must find the [[imperative]] in the sentence "Open your book." Then he has to add an [[apostrophe]] to the words "dont" and "cant." For physics, Dad's old [[barometer]] on the wall suddenly becomes useful, because the needle is falling fast. Taras learns that electric current is measured in [[amperes|ampere]], while the kettle uses about two [[kilowatts|kilowatt]]. Finally, Dad brings a [[micrometer]] from his toolbox, and Taras measures the thickness of a single hair. "This is the best homework ever," he says, just as the rain begins.

lessons.title: The science museum
lessons.story: On a rainy Saturday, Max takes his sister Sofia to the new science museum. At the entrance, a huge [[multimedia]] screen plays videos about our planet. Sofia stops in front of a real spacesuit once worn by a [[cosmonaut]]. In the next hall, an old [[microcomputer]] sits beside a photo of a modern [[supercomputer]] that fills a whole room. A guide explains that the big machine helps scientists predict the weather for the entire country. Then they walk through a cold, dark room that copies the Arctic [[tundra]], with recorded wind and tiny plants. The last exhibit is a map showing how the Indian [[subcontinent]] slowly crashed into Asia. Sofia begs to stay until closing time. On the way home, she announces that she is going to be a scientist, or maybe an astronaut.

lessons.title: Grandpa in the Hospital
lessons.story: In November, Anna's grandfather caught a bad cold that slowly turned into [[pneumonia]]. The doctors decided to keep him in the hospital for a week, and the nurses checked his [[pulse]] every few hours. Because of a flu outbreak, his ward was under [[quarantine]], so visitors could only talk to him by video call. The man in the next bed had spent two weeks in a [[coma]] after a car accident, but now he was sitting up and telling jokes. He said he was alive thanks to a blood [[donor]] he would never meet. That story impressed Anna so much that she decided to give blood as soon as she turned eighteen. Grandma, meanwhile, sent Grandpa bags of oranges, sure that [[vitamin]] C could cure anything. Grandpa laughed at her, but his [[optimism]] seemed to help more than any medicine. On Sunday, he came home, and the first thing he asked for was Grandma's soup.

lessons.title: A health talk at school
lessons.story: On Friday, a school nurse came to Anna's class to give a health talk. She started with [[nicotine]] and explained how quickly young people become addicted to it. Then she talked about harder drugs like [[cocaine]] and [[heroin]], which can destroy a life in a few months. Someone asked whether [[marijuana]] is safe, since it is legal in some countries. The nurse said it can still harm a teenage brain. She told them about a young man who spent a year in [[rehab]] before he finally got better. "For him, stress was the main [[trigger]]," she said, "so he learned new ways to relax." The second part of the talk was about the body and safe relationships, and she explained what a [[condom]] is and how it protects against infections. She even used a simple diagram of the [[penis]], and Max turned bright red. Afterward, Anna told him it was useful information, and he finally agreed.

lessons.title: A visit to the clinic
lessons.story: On Saturday morning, Anna took Taras to the clinic for his yearly [[checkup]]. Half the waiting room was coughing, because [[influenza]] was going around the city. The nurse put a [[thermometer]] under Taras's arm and said his temperature was normal. Taras admitted he never used [[floss]], so the doctor showed him how to clean between his teeth. Anna asked about her [[acne]], and the doctor recommended a gentle face wash. Their mama had come along too, because she wanted advice about the [[migraine]] she gets every few weeks. Their dad was there for a blood test, since the doctor wanted to check his [[cholesterol]] again. In the restroom, Anna noticed a basket of free pads and [[tampons|tampon]], which she thought was a kind idea. On the way home, Taras proudly showed everyone the sticker the doctor had given him.

lessons.title: The ambulance night shift
lessons.story: Max's sister Sofia works as a [[paramedic]] in Kyiv, and last week Max joined her for part of a night shift. At the station, the [[dispatcher]] sat in front of three screens and answered every call calmly. Sofia's partner, a former army [[medic]], drove the ambulance. Around midnight, Sofia's [[pager]] beeped, and they rushed to an elderly man with chest pain. She connected him to a heart monitor and explained that he needed constant [[monitoring]] on the way to the hospital. His wife mentioned nervously that he'd had [[laser]] surgery on his eyes a month earlier, so Sofia wrote that down too. On the drive back, she told Max about the [[lockdown]] in 2020, when the ambulances almost never stopped. Max had expected excitement, but mostly he saw tired people doing careful work. At six in the morning, Sofia bought him a coffee and said he had survived his first shift.

lessons.title: A hard road back
lessons.story: Ira's uncle Bohdan used to be a popular local football coach, until [[alcoholism]] slowly took away his job and his friends. For years he refused to admit that he was an [[alcoholic]]. Last winter, he finally went to a hospital for a week-long [[detox]], and Ira visited him every Sunday. He told her that the hardest part was a strange [[phobia]] of crowded rooms that he had developed while drinking. Little by little, he started going to support meetings and walking in the park every morning. In spring, a youth team asked him to help with training. On the field, he still moved by [[instinct]], shouting to the boys before they even saw the danger. In his first match, his team was losing 0–2 but made an amazing [[comeback]] and won 3–2. Ira and her friends cheered louder than anyone in the stands.

lessons.title: Grandpa and Grandma's checkup
lessons.story: Anna went with her grandparents to their family doctor, because both of them had a long list of questions. Grandpa started by complaining about a slight [[tremor]] in his hands. The doctor tested the [[reflex]] in his knee with a little hammer, and everything looked normal. Grandma had suffered from [[diarrhea]] for two days after a picnic, and the doctor suspected [[salmonella]] from the chicken salad. She didn't need an [[antibiotic]], just plenty of water and rest. Then Grandpa mentioned that he was allergic to [[penicillin]], so the doctor added a warning to his file. Anna asked whether [[zinc]] really helps against colds, and the doctor said it can, in small amounts. She also renewed the inhaler prescription for Taras, whose [[asthma]] gets worse in spring. Finally, Grandma proudly said she remembered getting the [[polio]] vaccine as a little girl. On the way out, Grandpa joked that he felt healthier just from talking about it.

lessons.title: In the hospital lab
lessons.story: Anna's biology class visited the lab at a big hospital in Kyiv. A friendly scientist let each student look at a drop of pond water under a [[microscope]]. Lisa was the first to spot an [[amoeba]], slowly changing its shape as it moved. The scientist explained that every [[microorganism]] in the drop was alive, even though none of them could be seen with the naked eye. "Not every [[microbe]] is dangerous," she added, "and many of them keep us healthy." Next, she showed them a [[tumor]] that a surgeon had removed that morning, and said that luckily it wasn't cancer. Max asked whether she had ever used a [[scalpel]], and she laughed and said only in medical school. She also told them about a boy whose [[appendix]] was removed last week and who was now recovering well. Before they left, she mentioned that the hospital runs a small [[hospice]] next door, where volunteers read to patients. Ira decided right there that she wanted to become one of those volunteers.

lessons.title: At the pharmacy
lessons.story: After a weekend at the lake, Lisa and Ira stopped at the pharmacy with a long list. Lisa had a bad sunburn, so the pharmacist gave her a bottle of cooling [[aloe vera]] gel. Ira laughed and said her grandma just cuts a leaf from the [[aloe]] on her windowsill. Ira had a headache, and the pharmacist suggested [[paracetamol]] because her stomach was already upset. "Don't take [[ibuprofen]] on an empty stomach," she warned. Lisa also needed some [[antiseptic]] for a cut on her foot from a sharp rock. Ira grabbed a small tin of [[vaseline]] for her dry lips. The pharmacist recommended a [[probiotic]] for Ira's stomach and asked whether she had eaten anything unusual. Ira admitted she had eaten a whole bag of peanuts, and the pharmacist joked that at least they weren't an [[allergen]] for her. The girls walked out laughing and promised to wear sunscreen next time.

lessons.title: The doctor's advice
lessons.story: Before visiting her grandparents, Anna woke up with a sore throat and took an [[antigen test]] just in case. It was negative, but she still went to see the family doctor with Max. The doctor said it was probably a cold, not the [[coronavirus]], and checked that Anna had had her [[diphtheria]] shot. Then she noticed that Anna's dad, who had driven them there, had paint on his hands. She told him to wear a [[respirator]] while he painted the kitchen. Max admitted that he had tried his cousin's [[vape]] at a party. The doctor didn't lecture him, but explained that [[vaping]] can damage young lungs and is hard to quit. In the hallway, Anna noticed a poster about free support for teens with [[bulimia]] and saved the phone number, just in case a friend ever needed it. On the way home, Max said he was glad he had only tried it once.

lessons.title: A relaxing weekend
lessons.story: After a stressful week of exams, Anna decided she needed a real break. Her mama suggested a weekend at a small [[spa hotel]] outside Kyiv, and Anna agreed to try a [[digital detox]] for two whole days. On Saturday morning, a calm instructor led a [[tai chi]] class in the garden, and Anna was surprised by how hard the slow movements were. Later, she and her mama visited the [[spa salon]] downstairs for a face treatment. In the afternoon, Anna took a long [[siesta]] instead of scrolling through her phone. On Sunday, they explored the [[wellness center]] next door, where Mama bought a small neck [[massager]] for Dad. When Anna finally turned her phone back on, she had forty messages from Max. She smiled, put the phone down, and answered them after dinner.

lessons.title: Max joins a gym
lessons.story: Max finally joined the new [[fitness center]] near his apartment. On his first day, a friendly [[trainer]] named Oleh showed him around and explained the equipment. Max wanted to build his [[biceps]] right away, but Oleh insisted on twenty minutes of [[cardio]] first. His sister Sofia, who goes there twice a week, was in the next room doing [[pilates]] with a group of older women. During the workout, Max kept checking the [[tracker]] on his wrist to see his heart rate. At the end, Oleh asked him to do one final [[sprint]] on the treadmill, and Max almost fell off. Sofia laughed and called Oleh a real fitness [[guru]]. Max wasn't so sure, but by the end of the month Oleh had become more of a [[mentor]] than a coach to him.

lessons.title: The big football match
lessons.story: On Friday, Anna's school team played in the city [[playoff]], and the whole class came to watch. The poster at the entrance said "School 52 [[versus]] School 14." Max, the team's best [[midfielder]], was nervous because the other team hadn't lost all season. In the first half, the referee called a [[foul]] against Max for a late tackle. A few minutes later, Max scored, but the goal didn't count because he was [[offside]]. Near the end, he gave a perfect [[assist]] to a teammate, who made it 1–1. The match went into [[extra time]], and the coach called a [[time-out]] to calm everyone down. Nobody scored again, and School 14 won on penalties. Still, the organizers gave Max's team the [[fair play]] award, and Anna said that was the best prize of all.

lessons.title: Game day at the arena
lessons.story: Lisa invited Anna to a basketball game at the new [[arena]] downtown. Lisa has been doing [[cheerleading]] for three years, and tonight she was performing in front of a big crowd for the first time. Before the game, the team [[mascot]], a giant blue owl, danced with the kids in the front row. All evening, Anna could hear the [[commentator]] getting more and more excited as the score stayed close. In the last second, a player threw the ball from the middle of the court, and it went in. The big screen showed the [[replay]] three times, and the crowd jumped up again each time. After the game, Lisa ran up to Anna, still in her uniform. "Did you see me?" asked the happiest [[cheerleader]] in the building. Anna nodded and said the winning shot was great, but Lisa's routine was the real [[highlight]] of the night.

lessons.title: A summer sports weekend
lessons.story: In July, Anna's family spent a long weekend by the sea near Odesa with her grandparents. On Saturday morning, Taras and Dad played [[frisbee]] on the beach until the sun got too hot. Anna watched a [[surfer]] ride a huge wave and decided she wanted to try it too. She rented a [[surfboard]], but she fell into the water about ten times in an hour. In the afternoon, she and Mama took a [[kayak]] along the coast, which was much easier. Meanwhile, Grandpa spent the day at the local [[golf club]], although he mostly sat in the café. That evening, Max called to say he had played [[paintball]] with Sofia and was covered in green paint. Later, they watched a [[polo]] match on TV, and Taras asked if they could go to a [[rodeo]] next. Instead, the next day they joined a friendly game of [[softball]] with another family, and Taras hit the ball over everyone's heads.

lessons.title: Fight night
lessons.story: On Saturday, Max took Anna and Ira to a local fight night at the sports center. The first match was [[MMA]], and Anna had to cover her eyes a few times. Ira, who has studied [[kung fu]] since she was six, explained every move to her. Then came the main event: a young [[boxer]] from Max's gym against a much taller man. His [[opponent]] looked confident, but the young fighter stayed calm and patient. In the third round, he landed one clean punch and won by [[knockout]]. On the way home, Anna admitted that fighting was a bit too intense for her. She suggested they watch [[sumo]] on TV next time, because the matches are short and nobody gets punched.

lessons.title: The Olympic dream
lessons.story: Anna's friend Lisa has been a [[gymnast]] since she was five, and she dreams of competing at the Olympics one day. Last weekend she took part in the national youth championship in Lviv, and Anna watched the live stream with her family. Lisa was the youngest [[finalist]] in the floor exercise. Her routine wasn't perfect, but she landed her final jump beautifully. When the scores came up, she had won bronze and become the first [[medalist]] from her sports school. Anna cried a little when Lisa stepped onto the [[podium]] with a huge smile. Grandpa, who used to run [[cross-country]] when he was young, said he had never been so proud. Then he announced that he was going to train for a [[triathlon]] at seventy, and everyone laughed.

lessons.title: Filming at the fitness club
lessons.story: Sofia has wanted to become a [[fitness blogger]] for months, so on Monday she filmed her first video at her [[fitness club]]. Max came along to hold the camera. First, Sofia compared her old [[fitness bracelet]] with her new [[smartwatch]] for her future viewers. The bracelet only counted steps, but the watch also worked as a full [[fitness tracker]], measuring her heart rate and sleep. Next, she showed a simple exercise for the [[triceps]] using just a chair. In the background, a huge [[bodybuilder]] was lifting weights, and Max kept filming him by accident. The man turned out to be very friendly and explained that he had switched to [[powerlifting]] last year. He even agreed to appear in the video, since he had once worked as a [[fitness model]]. When the video got two hundred views, Max joked that the real [[sportsman]] of the day was him, because he had held the camera for two hours.

lessons.title: Sports news
lessons.story: Max was writing the sports page for the school newspaper, and Anna offered to help. First came athletics: a local [[sprinter]] had broken the city record in the 100 meters. Then came football, where a striker from their school scored a [[hat trick]] thanks to some brilliant [[dribbling]]. The school [[futsal]] team had also won, and Sofia's [[water polo]] team finished second at the regional tournament. Anna added a short piece about the new [[squash]] courts near the metro. Max wanted to include betting odds from a [[bookmaker]], but Anna reminded him that most of their readers were under eighteen. Instead, they wrote about a racing driver whose slow [[pit stop]] had cost him the win, and about a boy from their street who came third in a [[motocross]] race. On Monday, the coach read the whole page aloud in the schoolyard through a [[megaphone]], and Max couldn't stop smiling.

lessons.title: Martial arts class
lessons.story: Lisa had been doing [[kickboxing]] for a year, and she finally convinced Anna to try a class at her gym. The coach, a former professional [[kickboxer]], started with a warm-up that left Anna completely out of breath. In the next room, a group was practicing [[aikido]], using their partners' energy instead of force. Lisa explained that she had also tried [[jiu-jitsu]], but she preferred fighting on her feet rather than on the floor. On the wall hung an old [[katana]], which the coach said had belonged to his own teacher. After class, Max turned up at the café downstairs and challenged both girls to [[arm wrestling]]. Lisa beat him in seconds, and Anna nearly did too. Max laughed and decided that maybe he should sign up for the beginner class as well.

lessons.title: Winter games
lessons.story: Anna's family spent the winter holidays at a small ski resort in the mountains. Every evening, Grandpa watched the winter games on TV and cheered for every athlete. On the first night, a Ukrainian skier came third in the [[slalom]], and Grandpa nearly jumped off the sofa. The next day, Taras insisted that the family ride down the hill on one long sled like a [[bobsleigh]] team, with Dad steering at the front. Mama preferred watching the [[biathlon]], although she admitted she would be terrible at both skiing and shooting. Meanwhile, a young [[snowboarder]] showed Anna how to come down the slope in a slow [[zigzag]] instead of going straight. By the afternoon, Taras and Grandma had built a small [[igloo]] behind the hotel. Grandpa crawled inside for a photo and declared it the best event of the whole winter.

lessons.title: An extreme weekend
lessons.story: For Max's birthday, Lisa and Ira planned an extreme weekend at an adventure park outside the city. Max had always said he wanted to try [[bungee jumping]], but when he saw the platform, he suddenly went quiet. So they started with the [[zipline]] instead, flying high above the trees while Sofia screamed with joy. Later, they watched a [[parachutist]] float slowly down and land right next to the parking lot. In the afternoon, they went [[kayaking]] on the lake, and Ira fell into the water twice. Their instructor turned out to run a local [[diving club]], and she invited them to a free trial lesson at the [[dive center]] next month. On Sunday, a professional [[stuntman]] gave a show, jumping a motorcycle over three cars. After that, some local teens showed off their [[parkour]] moves, and a [[skateboarder]] did a flip right in front of Max. On the way home, Max said it was his best birthday ever and promised to be braver next year.

lessons.title: The dog show
lessons.story: On Saturday, Anna and Max volunteered at the city dog show in the park. Their first job was to hold a sleepy [[bulldog]] that refused to walk into the ring. Next to them, a woman was brushing her white [[poodle]] until its fur looked like a cloud. A tiny [[terrier]] barked at everyone who walked past, including the judges. Meanwhile, a [[beagle]] escaped from its owner and followed the smell of sausages to the food tent. Max was nervous around a big [[pit bull]], but it turned out to be the friendliest dog at the show. Anna fell in love with a [[husky]] whose eyes were as blue as the sky. In the end, first prize went to a clever [[collie]] that did every trick perfectly. On the way home, Anna asked her mama for the hundredth time if they could get a dog.

lessons.title: Storm warning
lessons.story: One evening, a storm warning appeared on Anna's phone, so she and Ira stayed in and worked on their geography project about extreme weather. Ira explained how an earthquake under the ocean can cause a [[tsunami]] that reaches the coast within minutes. Anna found out that a [[typhoon]] and a [[cyclone]] are basically the same kind of storm, just with different names in different parts of the world. When the rain finally stopped, Dad looked out the window and said that at least the storm had cleared the [[smog]] over the city. That gave the girls an idea for a section on pollution and the [[ozone]] layer, which protects us from the sun's harmful rays. At the end, they added tips for an [[eco]] lifestyle, such as taking the metro and recycling plastic. On Friday, the teacher gave them the top grade, and Ira joked that their presentation had taken the class by storm.

lessons.title: A day at the zoo
lessons.story: Anna took Taras to the zoo for his birthday, and he made a list of every animal he wanted to see. First they found a [[leopard]] sleeping lazily on a branch, its tail hanging down. At the reptile house, Taras pressed his nose against the glass to look at an [[alligator]], which didn't move at all. A [[chameleon]] slowly turned from green to brown, while a huge [[python]] lay curled up under a heat lamp. Their favorite was a young [[orangutan]] who kept stealing his mother's banana. Next door, a [[lemur]] with a long striped tail jumped from rope to rope. In the insect house, a guide showed them a [[termite]] nest taller than Taras and a butterfly slowly breaking out of its [[cocoon]]. On the way out, they passed a bed of bright roses, and a sign explained that each one was a [[hybrid]] of two wild species. Taras checked off the last item on his list and announced that he wanted to be a zookeeper.

lessons.title: With the park ranger
lessons.story: During a summer exchange program in the American West, Anna and Max joined a guided hike in a national park. Their guide, a friendly [[ranger]] named Joe, promised them an amazing view from the [[peak]] before lunch. On the way up, he pointed at the deep red [[canyon]] below and explained that the river had been cutting it for millions of years. The trail passed huge gray rocks of [[granite]] and an old [[cedar]] that was older than the country itself. Near the top, Joe showed them black stones that had once been hot [[lava]]. He said they might hear a [[coyote]] at night, and that a herd of [[bison]] sometimes blocked the road near the entrance. Max nervously asked about dangerous animals, and Joe admitted that a [[puma]] had been seen nearby last spring. From the top, the park looked endless, and Joe said it covered more than a hundred thousand [[hectares|hectare]]. Max took dozens of photos, but he kept glancing at the bushes the whole way down.

lessons.title: Dogs in the Park
lessons.story: On Saturday, Anna and Max took Lisa's dogs to the park by the river. Lisa has a [[golden retriever]] called Sunny and a tiny [[corgi]] called Biscuit. Sunny jumped straight into the water, like every [[retriever]] does when it sees a lake. Biscuit tried to follow, but his short legs only got him as far as the mud.
